newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols slide after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols slide after jobs data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. stock indices dropped as the market firmed on mixed readings in the April U.S. employment report, traders said.
Trading in S&P 100 index options on the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) was hectic, with activity spread across a wide range of strike prices, traders said.

"It's typical," said an OEX trader of a brokerage firm. He noted that employment reports tended to be followed by a flurry of position squaring, although this week's rally was stimulating substantial fresh hedging and bullish speculative orders as well.
The CBOE volatility index, which reflect implied volatilities for near-month OEX options, was down 1.75 points at 19.77 at 1205 CDT/1705 GMT.

The Labor Department earlier said non-farm payrolls rose by 142,000 in April against an average Wall Street forecast of 211,000 and a revised 139,000 gain in March, while the jobless rate fell to 4.9 percent, the lowest level since 1973.
The slip in the unemployment rate surprised the market, but the mixed readings overall relieved some anxiety, traders said.
On the whole, traders said the market was looking positive. Contrarians particularly liked the heavy open interest accumulation in put options against a rising market.
"I think the right word is defiance," said Jerry Hegarty, an equity analyst at Thomson Financial Services. He expected the market to be bullish in the coming few weeks.

Joseph Sunderman, a research analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute, said open interest in May OEX puts increased by more than 30 percent this week to roughly 242,000 contracts at the end of Thursday, while call open interest rose only marginally to about 175,000.

In the OEX pit this morning, May 775 put was by far the most heavily traded option, with more than 9,600 contracts changing hands by mid-morning. Open interest in the May 775 put had nearly tripled on Thursday to 14,395 contracts.

Sunderman noted that more than 80 percent of the volume in that contract today appeared to have traded at the ask-side price, which could mean traders were still building up put positions aggressively.
Traders added that strength since Thursday in the technology sector, which had been lagging the broader market's blue chip-led bounce, was also positive.
"I think it's healthy to see...a broadening of the rally," Sunderman said. "You can't have that divergence for a really long period."
The Nasdaq 100 index was up 15.96 points at 898.08 at 1220 CDT/1720 GMT, with fairly good option traffic on CBOE.
NDX May 895 and 900 calls had volume of 1,166 and 822 contracts respectively, while May 810 and 850 puts had turnover of 1,009 and 1,483 respectively.
